plain: Tending to clear someone of blame or guilt.

webster.text: Able to clear from the charge of fault or guilt; excusing; containing excuse.

example.quote: And the wretched criminal, if he happen to have offended on the American side, stripped of his privilege of trial by peers of his vicinage, removed from the place where alone full evidence could be obtained, without money, without counsel, without friends, without exculpatory proof, is tried before judges predetermined to condemn.
example.cite: Thomas Jefferson, A Summary View of the Rights of British America, 1774
